Definition: the firstling of man or beast; abstractly primogeniture
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible bekorah means birthright, the right of the firstborn, and it appears 13 times across the Bible. Esau sold his birthright for a meal, Jacob took it, and Reuben's birthright passed to Joseph's sons.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the birthright mattered because it carried the blessing, and Esau's trade warns me never to sell what God gave me for a moment's appetite. That is why I keep coming back to it: bekorah is not a word to rush past.
